Maybe I just lack discipline, but it seems like I have a voracious appetite for reading in breaks from work/school, but the moment I have stuff to do that willpower is just gone. How do you guys find the discipline/motivation/anything to keep reading regularly, when you have a lot of things going on?
When your life starts to get busy, how do you get the motivation to keep reading regularly?

I read before bed most nights because I have trouble sleeping otherwise. It's now become such a part of my routine that it feels like I'm missing something if I don't read at night. Perhaps inserting some reading time to a daily routine of yours would help, even if it's just five minutes in the toilet or when having your morning coffee/breakfast/whatever.
Same here. Before bed is my regular routine. But if you're too tired, listen to your body.

I have a notebook in which I write a list of "Dailies" with checkboxes next to them (things like exercise, searching for work because I'm unemployed, practicing the ol' skinflute). One of my dailies is "read for 30 minutes". I usually end up reading for more than 30 minutes, but having a minimum daily "quota" kicks it off. The trick is to set the quota low enough that it doesn't feel like work - set it to a page or less a day if you want, it doesn't matter, it's just to get you to put the book in your hands and make you more likely to read.

By no means do I always get to check that box, but it always feels good when I do. I'm reading a lot more since I started doing that and it's great.

Read in between activities. That's what I do. When I'm waiting for something I will catch up on reading. You'd be surprised how much reading you get done that way. Carry a book in your pocket and then whip it out when you're in wait.

Take a night a week where you don't watch TV or get online. Make some tea, grab a blanket, and do it. One night a week, plan it out. Read smaller books too. Smaller books get into their story faster, and there is less to remember if you are only picking it up on occasions.

I find it relaxing to read out load. The main issue I've been having is that of reading fatigue in that I'll just feel really tired after having read only a few pages or so. Reading out load tends to fix this issue. Although by voice does get hoarse after an hour or so.

Some months ago, after a period of time when I wasn't doing any intentional reading for pleasure (only reading journal articles, reference books and the like) I decided to reread all the books I own in order to make my bookshelf more about quality over quantity. It's a long term goal, one that I know will take at least a couple of years, but I recently gave away my first donation of books and was pleasantly surprised to see how many books I've read since I started the project.

It's easy to say "make reading a priority" but you have to get more specific than that. Set a goal so small that you can't fail at it. Your first goal is to read for 2 minutes per day. It doesn't matter when, and it will probably be a different time every day, because you can squeeze 2 minutes in almost anywhere: you woke up before your alarm? Great, stay in bed, set the timer on your phone for 2 minutes and read. Traffic was light today and you got to work 6 minutes early? Fantastic sit in your car reading for 120 seconds and you still have 4 minutes to chitchat on the way to your desk. Your boss/teacher is running late to the meeting/class? Excellent, you don't have to talk to your neighbor, open your book and read until the meeting is called to order. You take your afternoon tea break and give yourself the luxury of 180 seconds to read while it steeps :) And the classic routine that has already been mentioned by others read for just 2 minutes right before you turn off the light at night.

Yes it means you're ending your reading mid paragraph or mid sentence but remember to keep your focus on the goal of reading regularly. So you succeed at this teeny tiny mini goal and now it's easy to expand it. Once you read 2 minutes per day for let's say ten days in a row, then you shift your goal slightly to reading 3 minutes once per day. Or change it to 2 minutes twice per day. The idea is just to make your goal so tiny you don't feel like you're putting in any effort at all. And if you're anything like me, you'll quickly find a way to make reading your go-to choice during any downtime. I carry the book I'm reading everywhere with me: in my bag, in my drawer at work, on my computer desk at home, and of course it ends each night on the bedside shelf.

I do hope you find a way to put books back into your life, I'm in love with feeling the same joy now in reading as I did when I was a child.
